reason: An `Identifier` value written in each round-trip format reads back as a `Literal` equal to `Literal("http://other.org/i", XSD_ANYURI)`. #526 and the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md`.

A document of every converted Python value reads back equal through each round-trip format, with the zero-duration row skipped for RDF. #482 and the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md`, and conformance caveat C10 for the skipped zero-duration row (#620).

An entity asserting an `Identifier` or a subclass of it stores `Literal(iri, XSD_ANYURI)`. #526 and the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md`, which store an `Identifier` as an `xsd:anyURI` literal.

An entity asserting an `xsd:decimal` literal with text `sNaN`, `NaN`, `Infinity` or `1e1`, an `xsd:boolean` `True` or an `xsd:int` `1.0` stores a `Literal` with the same text, equal to it and unequal to the same literal with a `0` appended. #593, #594 and #527, and the Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md`.

`ProvDocument.deserialize` of PROV-JSON holding the bare number 1.5 with `parse_float=decimal.Decimal` stores `Literal("1.5", XSD_DECIMAL)`. The Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md` stores a Decimal as an `xsd:decimal` Literal (#482), and `parse_float` is a declared PROV-JSON read option.

An entity asserting a tuple of 1000 integers raises `ProvValueError` whose message contains `...` and is under 200 characters. #482 asks for a clear error that names the attribute and the Python type. No source found for the length bound.
Serialising to PROV-O an entity that holds a decimal NaN or sNaN beside `0`, a decimal NaN beside a double, or a double NaN beside a decimal raises `decimal.InvalidOperation`. Conformance caveat C11.

A `Literal("1e1", XSD_DECIMAL)` written to PROV-O reads back as a `Literal` equal to `Literal("10", XSD_DECIMAL)` and unequal to `Literal("1e1", XSD_DECIMAL)`. Conformance caveat C10, which records that rdflib rewrites an exponent decimal on read.

An entity asserting a Decimal, date, time, timedelta, UUID, bytes, bytearray or memoryview value stores a `Literal` with the text and datatype given in each row. #482 and the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md`.

An entity asserting `Literal("ex:x", XSD_QNAME)` or `Literal("ex:x", PROV_QUALIFIEDNAME)` with `ex` declared stores a `QualifiedName` equal to `ex:x`. The Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md` stores a qualified-name literal whose prefix resolves as a `QualifiedName`, and release 3.3.0 design spec section 5.7.

A document holding `Literal("zz:x", XSD_QNAME)` in a bundle that declares `zz` reads back equal from PROV-JSON after `unified()`, `flattened()`, `update()` or `add_record()`. Release 3.3.0 design spec section 5.7 (a qualified-name value registers its namespace, so copies carry the prefix) and #526.

An entity asserting a str, int, bool, float, float subclass, datetime, `QualifiedName` or a `Literal` (language-tagged, decimal, date, or boolean `maybe`) holds a set equal to that one value under `==`, which does not tell `1` from `True`. #482 lists the supported types, and the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md` keeps these as they are.

An entity asserting a Fraction, complex, tuple, an opaque object, a non-finite Decimal or one whose exponent is out of range (1E+10000, 1E-10000), or a time with an offset that is not whole minutes or is beyond 14 hours raises `ProvValueError` with the message given in each row. #482 asks for a clear error that names the attribute and the Python type, and the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md` lists the rejected values.
